topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the scope of the lecture on cancer evolution and introduces the key learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic mechanisms in clonal selection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how intrinsic genetic mutations and epigenetic alterations confer selective advantages that drive clonal evolution in tissues.

topics.label: Stem cell hierarchies and cell of origin in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the relationship between normal tissue hierarchies and cancer stemness, providing evidence from leukemia and colorectal models.

topics.label: Microenvironmental promotion, inflammation, and stromal dependence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address how extrinsic microenvironmental signals, inflammatory responses, and supportive stroma cooperate with mutations to drive tumor growth and inform therapy.

topics.label: Experimental and computational methods for studying tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the laboratory models, sequencing technologies, and spatial profiling tools used to investigate tumor evolution and cellular interactions.

topics.label: Integrative evolutionary framework of cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesises the interplay of genetic mutations, epigenetic states, cell of origin, and microenvironmental factors into a unified evolutionary model of malignancy.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview of cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic marks the conclusion of the lecture and previews the following session on cancer therapy.
